summary: Two residential towers at 250 and 260 King Street, for which the Department of Building Inspection filed new-construction permits in November 2000 (17 stories each; 279 and 307 dwelling units) and recorded both as completed on 2004-10-06; the Assessor roll gives 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King Street, and two listing sites give 595 residential units and Catellus as developer.

milestones.text: Department of Building Inspection new-construction permit applications 200011306843 (250 King St: 17 stories, 279 dwelling units, mixed use) and 200011306844 (260 King St: 17 stories, 307 units, mixed use) filed, each with an estimated cost of $73,000,000

Department of Building Inspection records both new-construction permits as completed on 2004-10-06; the Assessor roll lists 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King St (listing sites say 2003)

facts.value: Permits propose 279 (250 King St) and 307 (260 King St) dwelling units, 586 together; two listing sites give 595 residential units. The counts are not reconciled.
17 on both permits; SFHighrises lists 16 floors and Afi + Associates 'two sixteen-story towers'
Catellus, per SFHighrises (listing-site profile; no primary source read)

open_questions: Developer is stated only by a listing site (SFHighrises); the Catellus Mission Bay page cited in the map's geometry file does not mention The Beacon. No primary source read confirms it.
Architect not recorded: Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; other attributions seen earlier by the project are unsourced here.

The permits do not use the name 'The Beacon'; the link from the name to 250 and 260 King St rests on the OpenStreetMap addr:housename tag cited in the geometry file and on SFHighrises and Afi + Associates, which both give 250 and 260 King St.
No construction start date or opening month found; the permit completed date is a closeout date, not an occupancy date.
The building permit for 260 King St has status 'reinstated' in the Department of Building Inspection data; the meaning is not explained in the data.
